channel.title: Abdur Rehman — ERP, Automation & AI Articles
channel.description: ERP developer in Pakistan building custom ERP software, AI assistants and automation for factories. See live projects, demo videos and real results.

item.title: 7 Signs Your Factory Has Outgrown Excel and Microsoft Access
item.description: Excel and Access work well for a small business. These seven signs show when they have started to cost you time, money and trust in your own numbers.

item.title: MS Access to MySQL Migration Without Losing Data
item.description: A real Microsoft Access to MySQL migration for a textile mill. What broke, how I fixed it, and the one rule that made the migration safe to run again and again.

item.title: What a Textile Mill ERP Must Track: From Greige to Dispatch
item.description: A textile processing mill is not a normal inventory business. Here is what an ERP has to track at every stage, from greige fabric receipt to packing and dispatch.

item.title: Custom ERP vs Ready-Made Software: How to Choose
item.description: Ready-made ERP is faster to start. Custom ERP fits the way you really work. A plain guide to choosing the right one for a growing factory or business.

item.title: Adding an AI Assistant to an ERP: What Really Works
item.description: How I built an assistant that answers staff questions from live ERP data by text or voice, keeps every permission, and never guesses a number.

item.title: Who Changed That Number? User Roles and Audit Trails in an ERP
item.description: One shared login is the most expensive shortcut in a business system. How proper user roles, server-side permissions and an audit trail protect your numbers.

item.title: A Backup You Have Never Tested Is Not a Backup
item.description: How to back up a business database properly: automatic, verified, off-site and cleaned up. The five-step nightly backup I run for a live factory ERP.

item.title: What Decides the Cost of Custom ERP Software?
item.description: Custom ERP has no fixed price list. These eight things decide what yours will cost, and here is how to keep the cost down without getting a weaker system.

item.title: Why I Built a Factory ERP on React, Express and MySQL
item.description: The architecture behind a live textile mill ERP: three options I considered, why boring technology won, and the single-server decision that mattered most.

item.title: How Much Is Where? Modelling a Multi-Stage Production Flow
item.description: The hardest part of a production ERP is not the code. It is the data model, and the transactions that stop a half-saved entry from quietly corrupting your reports.
